commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor Nova main flow into focused methods
commitResults.messageBody: Extract welcome rendering, command-loop processing, and goodbye rendering from Nova.main. The previous method combined several responsibilities and exceeded the code-quality guideline's warning threshold for long methods, making the program flow harder to scan and maintain. Named constants centralize the repeated divider, banner, and exit command values, while the extracted methods keep each section at a single level of abstraction. Preserve the existing command handling, output order, and scanner lifecycle.

Restrict Task's description and completion state to the Task class by changing both fields from protected to private. Neither Todo, Deadline, nor Event accesses these fields directly; they rely on Task's public behavior, so this preserves runtime behavior while preventing subclasses from coupling to the internal representation. This applies the code-quality guideline to minimize variable scope and strengthens encapsulation for future maintenance.

Consolidate the shared workflow used by the mark and unmark commands into updateTaskStatus. The previous implementations duplicated task-number parsing, task lookup, status updates, and user feedback, which made the two paths harder to maintain consistently and violated the DRY principle from the NUS code-quality guidelines. Keep the command-specific confirmation text and desired status at the call sites while centralizing the common workflow. Preserve the existing command behavior and output.

Make the Event time range and Deadline due date private and final. These fields are implementation details, and repository-wide usage confirms that no subclass or external class needs direct access to them. Restricting access prevents accidental mutation or coupling to the internal representation, while final fields communicate that these values are fixed after construction. Runtime behavior and task display output remain unchanged.
